analysis.title: EMEA UCITS ETP Flow Update, 19 October 2026
key_insights: EMEA UCITS ETPs took in $8.6B in the week of 08-14 Oct 2026, down from $13.6B the prior week. Equity, fixed income and commodity flows were all positive.
Equity ETP inflows were $6.1B vs $9.6B the prior week. Developed market equities took $6B and emerging markets took $103m.
Within developed markets, Global exposures took $3.9B (vs $4.8B prior week) and North America took $1.8B. DM APAC took $547m and DM Europe took $73m.

US equity ETPs took $1.8B, down from $3.4B the prior week. This was the third straight week of net inflows and brings YTD inflows to $64.4B. Japan ($281m), Switzerland ($246m) and Sweden ($64m) also saw inflows.
French equity ETPs saw outflows of $79m, the third straight week of net selling.
EM equity ETP inflows were $103m vs $193m prior week. Broad EM took $278m, EM single-country exposures lost $100m and regional exposures lost $75m.
Latin American ETPs lost $69m, the eighth straight week of outflows, bringing YTD outflows to $101m. China saw outflows of $340m vs $30m inflows the prior week. South Korea took $64m and Brazil $20m.
Active equity ETPs took $896m (vs $967m prior week), bringing YTD inflows to $23.5B. Alpha-seeking strategies took $713m (YTD $20.1B), led by Core at $665m.

Equity ESG ETPs took $218m (vs $244m prior week), YTD $17.8B. North American ESG lost $531m (fourth straight week of outflows) and EM ESG lost $207m (sixth straight week). ESG Optimised lost $593m while Screened took $365m.
Sector ETPs lost $553m, the second straight week of outflows, though YTD flows remain +$14.3B. European sectors lost $705m while US sectors gained $225m.
Financials lost $914m (vs $293m outflow prior week), bringing YTD to -$5.2B. European Financials accounted for -$734m of the weekly outflow.
Technology sector ETPs took $125m, Health Care $118m and Energy $90m. North American Technology took $74m.
Thematic ETPs took $247m (YTD $10.3B), led by Next Gen IT ($180m) and Robotics & AI ($161m). Climate Energy lost $83m and Fintech lost $32m.
Factor ETPs took $202m, the eighth straight week of inflows, YTD $9.7B. Quality led with $78m, followed by Momentum $53m, Multifactor $40m, Value $22m and Low volatility $8m.
Income strategies took $209m (eighth straight week of inflows, YTD $23.5B). Alternatives lost $32m after taking $207m the prior week.
Commodity ETPs took $56m vs $226m prior week. Gold took $170m (vs $489m prior), YTD $12.4B. Oil lost $102m and Silver lost $39m.
Fixed income ETPs took $2.5B vs $3.8B prior week. Investment grade led with $1.2B, about double its trailing 7-week average. Government took $813m (vs $2.3B prior week).
High yield flipped to $198m of inflows from -$72m. Inflation-linked took $143m and Broad Market $115m. EM debt lost $331m vs -$89m prior week, the main outlier, though it still has $5.2B YTD inflows.
Active fixed income: Exposure strategies took $225m after -$141m the prior week. Alpha-seeking lost $30m after seven straight weeks of inflows, with YTD at $6.2B.
Fixed income ESG: Investment grade took $522m (YTD $4.8B) and Government $114m. EM ESG debt lost $134m.
UCITS ETP dollar average daily volume was $20.7B (1.0x the 3-month average). Equity was $15.6B, fixed income $4.6B (1.1x) and commodities $0.5B (0.5x).

sector_views.rationale: Financials ETPs lost $914m in the week, led by European Financials at -$734m, with YTD flows at -$5.2B. This describes flows, not a bank view.
Technology ETPs took $125m, led by North America ($74m). Thematic flows favored Next Gen IT and Robotics & AI.

vol_and_positioning: Equity ETP flows were led by Global and US exposures while France, China and Latin America saw outflows.
Fixed income flows were broad-based and led by investment grade, with outflows from EM debt.
Gold ETP inflows slowed to $170m from $489m the prior week.
